title: Between proper and square coloring of planar graphs, hardness and extremal graphs
summary: $(1^a, 2^b)$-coloring is the problem of partitioning the vertex set of a graph into $a$ independent sets and $b$ 2-independent sets. This problem was recently introduced by Choi and Liu. We study the computational complexity and extremal properties of $(1^a, 2^b)$-coloring. We prove that this problem is NP-Complete even when restricted to certain classes of planar graphs, and we also investigate the extremal values of $b$ when $a$ is fixed and in some $(a + 1)$-colorable classes of graphs.
